description_full: Diversified Energy Company, an independent energy company, engages in the production, transportation and marketing of natural gas, oil, and liquids primarily in the Appalachian and Central regions of the United States. It also operates in the Bossier and Haynesville shale formations and the Cotton Valley sandstones in East Texas and West Louisiana, the Barnett Shale in North Texas and the Mid-Continent producing areas across Central Texas, along with the Anadarko Basin across North Texas and Oklahoma and Permian Basin in West Texas and New Mexico. Diversified Energy Company was founded in 2001 and is headquartered in Birmingham, Alabama.
ceo_bio: Mr. Robert Russell Hutson Jr. | Co-Founder, CEO & Chairman | Age 56 | Compensation: $2.2M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 1K people. Revenue per employee of $921K ranks in the below the sector median among Energy peers. Each employee generates $141K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $5K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 2× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (1/10).
financial_summary: Diversified Energy Company is a small-cap energy business with a $898M market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $280M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.36× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.1× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 9.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 4.6% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
